name: Wycliffe Bible, first complete English Vulgate
summary: Manuscripts of an early complete Middle English translation of the Latin Vulgate, associated with John Wycliffe and his Oxford circle, circulate from c. 1382. A revised version attributed to John Purvey follows c. 1395. The translation is later banned by Arundel's Constitutions (1409).

_quarry.structural_significance: First complete English Bible; despite official suppression, Wycliffite manuscripts circulate clandestinely and shape Lollard piety up to the 16th-century Reformation.
